Modern.tagline: The ger, rebuilt for the long stay.
Modern.brandNameRationale: Ger is the documented Mongolian word for the round felt-walled dwelling (the form Westerners call a yurt — yurt is Turkic, ger is Mongolian). 'Haus' is the German shorthand for a house brand. The compound reads as a modern travel brand grounded in the Mongolian tradition.
Modern.industrySummary: Modern glamping brands have split into the booking platforms (Hipcamp, Tentrr) and the operator brands (Under Canvas, Collective Retreats). The opening is for a modern operator brand sited on the Mongolian ger tradition — a documented dwelling form, not a marketing tent.
Modern.competitorLandscape: Under Canvas (undercanvas.com) is the modern operator peer at scale. Collective Retreats (collectiveretreats.com) holds the design-led modern slot. Hipcamp (hipcamp.com) is the booking-platform middle. AutoCamp (autocamp.com) plays the Airstream-modern peer. We sit closer to Collective Retreats with a ger specialism.
Modern.positioningStatement: Modern ger camps for the long stay.

targetAudience.primary: 30 to 50. Books for a week, not a night. Brings the laptop and the book. Reads the property's land story.
behaviors: Reads the land history before booking

dos: List what's on the land — wood-fired stove, well water
donts: Use the word glamping in primary copy

Modern.logoDirection: A wordmark — Gerhaus in a precise modern grotesque, with a small circular ger-roof glyph above that reads as a felt-roof crown in plan view.

typography.secondary: GT America Mono for stay codes and check-in times
typography.rationale: The mono carries the booking. The regular carries the brand.

Luxury.tagline: The hunting-lodge tradition, at the treeline.
Luxury.brandNameRationale: The Indian maharaja hunting lodges of the 19th and early 20th century (Sawai Madhopur, Ranthambore, Sariska) are the documented heritage anchor for luxury tented camping — silver service, Persian rugs, cotton drill tents. 'Pine' places the brand at the treeline, the geographic register of mountain luxury. The pairing reads as a heritage hunting-camp brand without naming any single dynasty.
Luxury.industrySummary: Luxury glamping sits inside operators like &Beyond, Singita, Belmond Safaris — predominantly African. The opening is for a Himalayan-and-temperate luxury tented camp brand drawing on the Indian maharaja tradition rather than the African safari tradition.
Luxury.competitorLandscape: Aman (aman.com) holds the luxury-tented peer slot, particularly Amanbagh. Singita (singita.com) plays the safari-luxury reference. Belmond Safaris (belmond.com) sits in the global heritage luxury middle. We belong with Aman, in the Indian register.
Luxury.positioningStatement: A heritage hunting-lodge brand for tented camps at the treeline.

targetAudience.primary: 45 to 70. Books a week. Travels with a butler. Reads the property's heritage paper before arrival.

dos: Confirm by hand-written card on cotton stock
Print the seasonal program in the dak booklet
donts: Photograph the tent's exterior at dusk

Luxury.logoDirection: A serif wordmark — Maharaja & Pine in a classical book serif with a small embossed elephant-and-pine mark on the dak booklet.

typography.primary: A traditional book serif for the wordmark and dak booklet
typography.secondary: An engraver's italic for the chamberlain's signature

Minimal.brandNameRationale: Yurt is the documented Turkic word for the round felt dwelling, in common English use since the 19th century. 'House' is the smallest accommodation suffix. The brand names the form and stops there.
Minimal.industrySummary: Most glamping brands accumulate property types — bell tents, treehouses, geodesic domes, safari tents, Airstreams. There's an opening for a brand that offers one form at one price.
Minimal.competitorLandscape: Most operators fail this purity test. The closest peers in spirit are some single-form Mongolian camps and certain old-school Lakeland bothies.

targetAudience.primary: Guests who already know they want a yurt and want the dates, the price, and the booking link.
behaviors: Books one yurt for two nights

dos: Show the yurt, the dates, the price

Minimal.logoDirection: Yurt House set in a single-weight grotesque, lowercase. The mark appears on the door, the receipt, and nowhere else.

typography.rationale: One face. The door, the receipt, the booking page share the same mark.

Corporate.brandNameRationale: Canvas is the documented material of the tented-camp tradition (cotton drill, used in safari and maharaja camps since the 19th century). The word is generic and clear of TM. 'Hospitality' is the standard corporate operator suffix (Hyatt Hospitality, Hilton Hospitality). The pairing reads as a serious tented-hospitality operator without colliding with the Canopy by Hilton trademark.
Corporate.industrySummary: Tented hospitality at operator scale — luxury tented camps supplied to hotel groups, REITs, and tourism boards — is a B2B category dominated by mid-tier operators (Under Canvas, Collective Retreats at scale, AutoCamp). The opening is a corporate operator with multi-property capacity and operator-grade reliability.
Corporate.competitorLandscape: Under Canvas (undercanvas.com) is the institutional peer at scale. Collective Retreats (collectiveretreats.com) holds the design-led operator slot. AutoCamp (autocamp.com) plays the Airstream-portfolio peer. We sit alongside Under Canvas with a broader form catalog.
Corporate.positioningStatement: Multi-property tented hospitality for hotel groups and tourism boards.

targetAudience.primary: Hotel-group development directors, REIT acquisition teams, and tourism-board procurement leads sourcing tented hospitality at scale.
motivations: A serious operator with hospitality-grade reliability

dos: Lead with property counts and RevPAR data
Show case studies with named hotel-group partners

messagingPillars.name: Operator capability
messagingPillars.description: Multi-property tented hospitality with full BOH, F&B, and housekeeping at hospitality standard.

messagingPillars.name: Code-compliant
messagingPillars.description: All structures engineered to local code with full permitting and inspection trail.

messagingPillars.name: Partner support
messagingPillars.description: Dedicated programs for hotel groups and tourism boards.

Corporate.logoDirection: A wordmark with a small geometric mark to the left — a single tent-peak silhouette. Reads cleanly on a spec deck and shipping case.

typography.primary: Inter for marketing and B2B materials
typography.secondary: Source Serif Pro for printed contracts and operator manuals
typography.rationale: Inter scales clean across digital. The serif handles printed contracts.

Creative.tagline: A camp that moves with the season.
Creative.brandNameRationale: The maharaja hunting-camp tradition (Indian princely states, 19th–early 20th century) involved moving the camp with the seasons — cool-weather Sariska, monsoon Ranthambore. The Wandering prefix names the migration. The pairing reads as a warm, character-driven camp house with a documented historical anchor.
Creative.manifesto: Most glamping brands sell the night. We sell the season. The camp that moves up to the cool meadow in May and down to the river fork in October. The brand is for the long traveller, not the weekend tourist.
Creative.industrySummary: Glamping branding has been polished, Instagram-ready, and a little cold. There's room for one that's warm, narrative, character-driven, and serious about the migratory camp tradition.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Collective Retreats (collectiveretreats.com) does the design-led institutional middle. Singita (singita.com) holds the heritage-narrative peer slot. Hipcamp (hipcamp.com) sits in the booking-platform peer position. We sit warmer and more migratory than any of them.
Creative.positioningStatement: A migratory camp brand for the long traveller.

targetAudience.primary: 35 to 60. Books for two weeks. Brings the children. Reads the camp's seasonal program before arrival.

dos: Photograph the camp during the move
Tell the story of the season, not the night
Send a natural-history note with each booking

Creative.logoDirection: A wordmark in a punchy display serif with a small elephant-on-pack glyph replacing the article. The elephant stands alone on the dak card and the sticker.

typography.primary: Migra for the wordmark and big display
typography.secondary: PP Neue Montreal for body and seasonal program notes
typography.rationale: Migra has personality. Neue Montreal handles the program.
